verses.1: And now hear me, my children, what things I saw concerning the seven spirits of deceit, when I repented.
verses.2: Seven spirits therefore are appointed against man, and they are the leaders in the works of youth.
verses.3: [And seven other spirits are given to him at his creation, that through them should be done every work of man,
verses.4: The first is the spirit of life, with which the constitution (of man) is created. The second is the sense of sight, with which ariseth desire.
verses.5: The third is the sense of hearing, with which cometh teaching. The fourth is the sense of smell, with which tastes are given to draw air and breath.
verses.6: The fifth is the power of speech, with which cometh knowledge.
verses.7: The sixth is the sense of taste, with which cometh the eating of meats and drinks; and by it strength is produced, for in food is the foundation of strength.
verses.8: The seventh is the power of procreation and sexual intercourse, with which through love of pleasure sins enter in.
verses.9: Wherefore it is the last in order of creation, and the first in that of youth, because it is filled with ignorance, and leadeth the youth as a blind man to a pit, and as a beast to a precipice.

verses.1: And Reuben died, having given these commands to his sons.
verses.2: And they placed him in a coffin until they carried him up from Egypt, and buried him in Hebron in the cave where his father was.

verses.1: The copy of the words of Simeon, the things which he spake to his sons before he died, in the hundred and twentieth year of his life, at which time Joseph, his brother, died.
verses.2: For when Simeon was sick, his sons came to visit him, and he strengthened himself and sat up and kissed them, and said:—

verses.1: And the sons of Simeon bewailed their father.
verses.2: And they were in Egypt until the day of their departure by the hand of Moses.

verses.1: The copy of the words of Levi, the things which he ordained unto his sons, according to all that they should do, and what things should befall them until the day of judgment.
verses.2: He was sound in health when he called them to him; for it had been revealed to him that he should die. And when they were gathered together he said to them:

verses.1: And I said to my father Jacob: By thee will Yahuah (Lord) destroy the Canaanites, and will give their land to thee and to thy seed after thee.
verses.2: For from this day forward shall Shechem be called a city of imbeciles; for as a man mocketh a fool, so did we mock them,
verses.3: Because also they had wrought folly in Yashar'el (Israel) by defiling my sister. And we departed and came to Bethel.

verses.1: Therefore when I took a wife I was twenty-eight years old, and her name was Melcha.
verses.2: And she conceived and bare a son, and I called his name Gersam, for we were sojourners in our land.
verses.3: And I saw concerning him, that he would not be in the first rank.
verses.4: And Kohath was born in the thirty-fifth year of my life, towards sunrise.
verses.5: And I saw in a vision that he was standing on high in the midst of all the congregation.
verses.6: Therefore I called his name Kohath [which is, beginning of majesty and instruction].
verses.7: And she bare me a third son, Merari, in the fortieth year of my life; and since his mother bare him with difficulty, I called him Merari, that is my bitterness, because he also was like to die.
verses.8: And Jochebed was born in Egypt, in my sixty-fourth year, for I was renowned then in the midst of my brethren.

verses.1: And Gersam took a wife, and she bare to him Lomni and Semei.
verses.2: And the sons of Kohath, Ambram, Issachar, Hebron, and Ozeel.
verses.3: And the sons of Merari, Mooli and Mouses.
verses.4: And in my ninety-fourth year Ambram took Jochebed my daughter to him to wife, for they were born in one day, he and my daughter.
verses.5: Eight years old was I when I went into the land of Canaan, and eighteen years when I slew Shechem, and at nineteen years I became priest, and at twenty-eight years I took a wife, and at forty-eight I went into Egypt.
verses.6: And behold, my children, ye are a third generation.
verses.7: In my hundred-and-eighteenth year Joseph died.

verses.1: Therefore the temple, which Yahuah (Lord) shall choose, shall be laid waste through your uncleanness, and ye shall be captives throughout all nations.
verses.2: And ye shall be an abomination unto them, and ye shall receive reproach and everlasting shame from the righteous judgment of Elohim (God).
verses.3: And all who hate you shall rejoice at your destruction.
verses.4: And if you were not to receive mercy through Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, our fathers, not one of our seed should be left upon the earth.

verses.1: And whereas ye have heard concerning the seventy weeks, hear also concerning the priesthood.
verses.2: For in each jubilee there shall be a priesthood. And in the first jubilee, the first who is anointed to the priesthood shall be great, and shall speak to Elohim (God) as to a father. And his priesthood shall be perfect with Yahuah (Lord), [and in the day of his gladness shall he arise for the salvation of the world].
verses.3: In the second jubilee, he that is anointed shall be conceived in the sorrow of beloved ones; and his priesthood shall be honoured and shall be glorified by all.
verses.4: And the third priest shall be taken hold of by sorrow.
verses.5: And the fourth shall be in pain, because unrighteousness shall gather itself against him exceedingly, and all Yashar'el (Israel) shall hate each one his neighbour.
verses.6: The fifth shall be taken hold of by darkness.
verses.7: Likewise also the sixth and the seventh.
verses.8: And in the seventh shall be such pollution as I cannot express before men, for they shall know it who do these things.
verses.9: Therefore shall they be taken captive and become a prey, and their land and their substance shall be destroyed.
verses.10: And in the fifth week they shall return to their desolate country, and shall renew the house of Yahuah (Lord).
verses.11: And in the seventh week shall come priests, (who are) idolaters, adulterers, lovers of money, proud, lawless, lascivious, abusers of children and beasts.

verses.1: And Yahuah (Lord) showed me favour in all my works both in the field and in the house.
verses.2: I know that I raced a hind, and caught it, and prepared the meat for my father, and he did eat.
verses.3: And the roes I used to master in the chase, and overtake all that was in the plains. A wild mare I overtook, and caught it and tamed it.
verses.4: I slew a lion and plucked a kid out of its mouth. I took a bear by its paw and hurled it down the cliff, and it was crushed.
verses.5: I outran the wild boar, and seizing it 'as I ran', I tare it in sunder.
verses.6: A leopard in Hebron leaped upon my dog, and I caught it by the tail, and hurled it on the rocks, and it was broken in twain.
verses.7: I found a wild ox feeding in the fields, and seizing it by the horns, and whirling it round and stunning it, I cast it from me and slew it.

verses.1: And when the two kings of the Canaanites came sheathed in armour against our flocks, and much people with them, single-handed I rushed upon the king of Hazor, and smote him on the greaves and dragged him down, and so I slew him.
verses.2: And the other, the king of Tappuah, as he sat upon his horse, [I slew, and so I scattered all his people.
verses.3: Achor the king] a man of giant stature 'I found', hurling javelins before and behind as he sat on horseback, and I took up a stone of sixty pounds weight, and hurled it and smote his horse, and killed it.
verses.4: And I fought with (this) other for two hours; and I clave his shield in twain, and I chopped off his feet, and killed him.
verses.5: And as I was stripping off his breastplate, behold nine men his companions began to fight with me.
verses.6: And I wound my garment on my hand; and I slung stones at them, and killed four of them, and the rest fled.
verses.7: And Jacob my father slew 'Beelesath, king' of all the kings, a giant in strength, twelve cubits high.
verses.8: And fear fell upon them, and they ceased warring against us.
verses.9: Therefore my father was free from anxiety in the wars when I was with my brethren.
verses.10: For he saw in a vision 'concerning me' that an angel of might followed me everywhere, that I should not be overcome.

verses.1: And in the south there came upon us a greater war than that in Shechem; and I joined in battle array with my brethren, and pursued a thousand men, and slew of them two hundred men and four kings.
verses.2: And I went up upon the wall, and I slew four mighty men.
verses.3: And so we captured Hazor, and took all the spoil.

verses.1: On the next day we departed to Aretan, a city strong and walled and inaccessible, threatening us with death.
verses.2: But I and Gad approached on the east side of the city, and Reuben and Levi on the west.
verses.3: And they that were upon the wall, thinking that we were alone, 'were drawn down' against us.
verses.4: And so my brothers secretly climbed up the wall on both sides by stakes, and entered the city, while the men knew it not.
verses.5: And we took it with the edge of the sword. And as for those who had taken refuge in the tower, we set fire to the tower and took both it and them.
verses.6: And as we were departing the men of Tappuah seized our spoil, and seeing (this) we fought with them.
verses.7: And we slew them all and recovered our spoil.

verses.1: And when I was at the waters of Kozeba, the men of 'Jobel' came against us to battle.
verses.2: And we fought with them and routed them; 'and their allies from Shiloh we slew,' and we did not leave them 'power' to come in against us.
verses.3: And the men of 'Makir' came upon us the fifth day, to seize our spoil; and we attacked them and overcame them in fierce battle: for there was a host of mighty men amongst them, and we slew them before they had gone up the ascent.
verses.4: And when we came to their city their women rolled upon us stones from the brow of the hill on which the city stood.
verses.5: And I and Simeon hid ourselves behind the town, and seized upon the heights, and destroyed this city also.

verses.1: And the next day it was told us that the king of the city of Gaash with a mighty host was coming against us.
verses.2: I, therefore, and Dan feigned ourselves to be Amorites, and as allies went into their city.
verses.3: And in the depth of night our brethren came and we opened to them the gates; and we destroyed all the men and their substance, and we took for a prey all that was theirs, and their three walls we cast down.
verses.4: And we drew near to Thamna, where was all the substance of the hostile kings.
verses.5: Then being insulted by them, I was therefore wroth, and rushed against them to the summit; and they kept slinging against me stones and darts.
verses.6: And had not Dan my brother aided me, they would have slain me.
verses.7: We came upon them, therefore, with wrath, and they all fled; and passing by another way, they besought my father, and he made peace with them.
verses.8: And we did to them no hurt, and they became tributary to us, and we restored to them their spoil.
verses.9: And I built Thamna, and my father built Rabael.
verses.10: I was twenty years old when this war befell.
verses.11: And the Canaanites feared me and my brethren.

verses.1: And I had much cattle, and I had for chief herdsman Iram the Adullamite.
verses.2: And when I went to him I saw Barsaba, king of Adullam; 'and he spake unto us', and he made us a feast; and when I was heated he gave me his daughter Bathshua to wife.
verses.3: She bare me Er, and Onan, and Shelah; and two of them Yahuah (Lord) smote: for Shelah lived, and his children are ye.

verses.1: And eighteen years my father abode at peace with his brother Esau, and his sons with us, after that we came from Mesopotamia, from Laban.
verses.2: And when eighteen years were fulfilled, in the fortieth year of my life, Esau, the brother of my father, came upon us with a mighty and strong people.
verses.3: And Jacob smote Esau with an arrow, and he was taken up wounded on Mount Seir, and as he went he died at Anoniram.
verses.4: And we pursued after the sons of Esau. Now they had a city with walls of iron and gates of brass; and we could not enter 'into it', and we encamped around, and besieged it.
verses.5: And when they opened not to us in twenty days, I set up a ladder 'in the sight of all', and with my shield upon my head I went up, sustaining the assaults of stones, upwards of three talents weight; and I slew four of their mighty men.
verses.6: And Reuben and Gad slew six others.
verses.7: Then they asked from us terms of peace; and having taken counsel with our father, we received them as tributaries.
verses.8: And they gave us five hundred cors of wheat, five hundred baths of oil, five hundred measures of wine, 'until the famine,' when we went down into Egypt.

verses.1: The copy of the words of Issachar. For he called his sons and said to them: Hearken, my children, to Issachar your father; Give ear to the words of him who is beloved of Yahuah (Lord).
verses.2: I was born the 'fifth son to Jacob', by way of hire for the mandrakes.
verses.3: For Reuben 'my brother' brought in mandrakes from the field, and Rachel met him and took them.
verses.4: And Reuben wept, and at his voice Leah my mother came forth.
verses.5: Now these (mandrakes) were 'sweet-smelling' apples which were produced in the land of Haran below a ravine of water.
verses.6: And Rachel said: I will not give them to thee, but they shall be to me instead of children. 'For Yahuah (Lord) hath despised me, and I have not borne children to Jacob'.
verses.7: Now there were two apples; and Leah said 'to Rachel': Let it suffice thee that thou hast taken my husband: wilt thou take these also?
verses.8: And Rachel said 'to her': Thou shalt have Jacob this night for the mandrakes 'of thy son'.
verses.9: And Leah said to her: Jacob is mine, for I am the wife of his youth.
verses.10: But Rachel said: Boast not, and vaunt not thyself; for he espoused me before thee, and for my sake he served our father fourteen years.
verses.11: And had not craft increased on the earth and the wickedness of men prospered, thou wouldest not now see the face of Jacob.
verses.12: For thou art not his wife, but in craft wert taken to him in my stead.
verses.13: And my father deceived me, 'and removed me on that night,' and did not suffer 'Jacob to see me; for' had I been there, this had not happened 'to him'.
verses.14: Nevertheless, for the mandrakes I am hiring Jacob to thee for one night.
verses.15: And Jacob knew Leah, and she 'conceived and' bare me, and on account of the hire I was called Issachar.

verses.1: Then appeared to Jacob an angel of Yahuah (Lord), saying: Two children shall Rachel bear, inasmuch as she hath refused company with her husband, and hath chosen continency.
verses.2: And had not Leah my mother paid the two apples for the sake of his company, she would have borne eight sons; for this reason she bare six, and Rachel bare the two: for on account of the mandrakes Yahuah (Lord) visited her.
verses.3: For He knew that for the sake of children she wished to company with Jacob, and not for lust of pleasure.
verses.4: For on the morrow also she again gave up Jacob. Because of the mandrakes, therefore, Yahuah (Lord) hearkened to Rachel.
verses.5: For though she desired them, she eat them not, but offered them in the house of Yahuah (Lord), presenting them to the priest of the El Elyon (Most High) who was at that time.

verses.1: For anger is an evil thing, my children, for it troubleth even the soul itself.
verses.2: And the body of the angry man it maketh its own, and over his soul it getteth the mastery, and it bestoweth upon the body 'power that it may work all' iniquity.
verses.3: And when the body does all these things, the soul justifieth what is done, since it seeth not aright.
verses.4: Therefore he who is wrathful, if he be a mighty man, hath a threefold power in his anger: one by the help of his servants; and a second by his wealth, whereby he persuadeth and overcometh wrongfully; and thirdly, having his own natural power he worketh thereby the evil.
verses.5: And though the wrathful man be weak, yet hath he a power twofold of that which is by nature; for wrath ever aideth such in lawlessness.
verses.6: This spirit goeth always with lying 'at the right hand of Satan, that with cruelty and lying' his works may be wrought.

verses.1: And when he had said these things he kissed them, and fell asleep at a good old age.
verses.2: And his sons buried him. And after that they carried up 'his bones', and placed them near Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob.
verses.3: [Nevertheless, 'Dan' prophesied unto them that they should forget their Elohim (God), and should be alienated from the land of their inheritance 'and from the race of Israel', and from the family of 'their seed'.]

verses.1: These two dreams I told to my father; and he said to me: These things must be fulfilled in their season, after that Yashar'el (Israel) hath endured many things.
verses.2: Then my father saith unto me: I believe Elohim (God) that Joseph liveth, for I see 'always' that Yahuah (Lord) numbereth him with you.
verses.3: And he said, weeping: Ah me, my son, Joseph, thou livest, though I behold thee not, and thou seest not Jacob that begat thee.
verses.4: He caused me also, therefore, to weep by these words, and I burned in my heart to declare that 'Joseph' had been sold, but I feared my brethren.

verses.1: And when he had charged them with many such words, he exhorted them that they should remove his bones to Hebron, and that they should bury him with his fathers.
verses.2: And when he had eaten and drunken with a merry heart, he covered his face and died.
verses.3: And his sons did according to all that Naphtali their father had commanded them.

verses.1: And when he had said these things unto them, he commanded saying: Bury me in Hebron. And he fell asleep and died at a good old age.
verses.2: And his sons did as he had commanded them, and they carried him up to Hebron, and buried him with his fathers.

verses.1: 'And' again, at another time she said unto me: If thou wilt not commit adultery, I will kill my husband by poison, and take thee to be my husband.
verses.2: I therefore, when I heard this, rent my garments, and said unto her: Woman, reverence Elohim (God), and do not this evil deed, lest thou be destroyed; for know indeed that I will declare this thy device unto all men.
verses.3: She therefore, being afraid, besought that I would not declare this device.
verses.4: And she departed, soothing me with gifts, and sending to me every delight of the sons of men.

verses.1: But her heart was still set upon evil, and she looked around how to ensnare me, and sighing deeply she became downcast, though she was not sick.
verses.2: And when her husband saw her, he said unto her: Why is thy countenance fallen? And she said 'unto him': I have a pain at my heart, and the groanings of my spirit oppress me; and so he comforted her who was not sick.
verses.3: Then accordingly seizing an opportunity she rushed unto me while her husband was yet without, and said unto me: I will hang myself, or cast myself over a cliff, if thou wilt not lie with me.
verses.4: And when I saw the spirit of Beliar was troubling her, I prayed unto Yahuah (Lord), and said unto her:
verses.5: Why, 'wretched woman', art thou troubled and disturbed, blinded through sins? Remember that if thou kill thyself, Asteho, the concubine of thy husband, thy rival, will beat thy children, and thou wilt destroy thy memorial from off the earth.
verses.6: And she said unto me: Lo, then thou lovest me; let this suffice me: only strive for my life 'and my children', and I expect that I shall enjoy my desire 'also'.
verses.7: But she knew not that because of my lord I spake thus, and not because of her.
verses.8: For if a man hath fallen before the passion of a wicked desire and become enslaved by it, even as she, whatever good thing he may hear with regard to that passion, he receiveth it with a view to his wicked desire.

verses.1: And about that time the Memphian woman, the wife of Pentephri, came down 'in a chariot', 'with great pomp, because she had heard from her eunuchs concerning me'.
verses.2: And she told her husband that the merchant had become rich by means of a young Hebrew, and they say that he had assuredly been stolen out of the land of Canaan.
verses.3: Now, therefore, render justice unto him, and take away the youth to thy house; so shall the Elohim (God) of the Hebrews bless thee, for grace from heaven is upon him.

verses.1: And Pentephris was persuaded by her words, and commanded the merchant to be brought, and said unto him: What is this that I hear 'concerning thee', that thou stealest persons out of the land of Canaan, and sellest them for slaves?
verses.2: But the merchant fell at his feet, and besought him, saying: I beseech thee, my lord, I know not what thou sayest.
verses.3: And Pentephris said unto him: Whence, then, is the Hebrew slave? And he said: The Ishmaelites entrusted him to me until they should return.
verses.4: But he believed him not, but commanded him to be stripped and beaten. And when he persisted in this statement, Pentephris said: Let the youth be brought.
verses.5: And when I was brought in, I did obeisance to Pentephris (for he was third in rank of the officers of Pharaoh).
verses.6: And he took me apart from him, and said unto me: Art thou a slave or free? And I said: A slave.
verses.7: And he said: Whose? And I said: The Ishmaelites'.
verses.8: And he said: How didst thou become their slave? And I said: They bought me out of the land of Canaan.
verses.9: And he said unto me: 'Truly' thou liest; and 'straightway' he commanded me to be stripped and beaten.

verses.1: Now the Memphian woman was looking through a window 'at me while I was being beaten, for her house was near, and she sent unto him, saying': Thy judgment is unjust; for thou dost punish a 'free' man who hath been stolen, as though he were a transgressor.
verses.2: And when I made no change in my statement, 'though I was beaten', he ordered me to be imprisoned, until, he said, the owners of the boy should come.
verses.3: And the woman said unto her husband: Wherefore dost thou detain the captive and well-born lad in bonds, who ought rather to be set at liberty, and be waited upon?
verses.4: For she wished to see me out of a desire 'of sin', but I was ignorant concerning all these things.
verses.5: And he said to her: It is not the custom of the Egyptians to take away that which belongeth to others before proof is given.
verses.6: This, therefore, he said concerning the merchant; but as for the lad, he must be imprisoned.

verses.1: Now the Memphian woman said to her husband: Buy the youth; for I hear, said she, that they are selling him.
verses.2: And 'straightway' she sent a eunuch to the Ishmaelites, and asked them to sell me.
verses.3: But since the eunuch would not agree to buy me (at their price) he returned, having made trial of them, and he made known to his mistress that they asked a large price for their slave.
verses.4: And she sent another eunuch, saying: Even though they demand two minae, 'give them', do not spare 'the gold'; only buy the boy, and bring him to me.
verses.5: The eunuch therefore went and gave them eighty pieces of gold, and 'he received me'; but to the Egyptian woman he said: I have given a hundred.
verses.6: And though I knew (this) I held my peace, lest the eunuch should be put to shame.

Until He shall again visit you and in pity receive you

Choose the light or the darkness — the witnesses called
Judah — the fourth son, named for thanksgiving, blessed to be king
Er and Onan — slain for their wickedness against Tamar

Tamar by the gate — the staff, the girdle, and the pledge
Drunk with wine — the root of the abomination in Israel
Keep the ordinances of Yahuah — walk not after your lusts
The wine turned aside my eyes — pleasure blinded my heart
Be not drunk with wine — it turns the mind from truth
Even a king is stripped of his kingship by fornication
Drink in gladness with the fear of Elohim — or touch it not at all
Love not money nor the beauty of women — the twin snares
From me shall the kingdom be established — the Davidic covenant
Fornication and the love of money withdraw a man from the law
The love of money leadeth to idolatry
Two spirits wait upon man — the heart known to Yahuah
Love Levi — the priesthood set higher than the kingdom
The kings as sea-monsters and the false prophets like tempests
Until the salvation of Israel and the Elohim of righteousness appear
Scattered for sin — until Yahuah visit you when ye repent

The heavens opened upon Him — the Spirit poured out
This Branch of Elohim — the Fountain giving life unto all

Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob shall arise unto life
Beliar cast into the fire for ever — one people of Yahuah

Carried up to Hebron — buried with his fathers
Issachar the husbandman — walking in singleness of eye
First-fruits offered, the poor sustained

Keep the law — love the Lord and thy neighbour

Levi and Judah — the priesthood and the kingdom
Dispersed among the Gentiles, brought back to their land
Guile arose not in my heart
I loved the Lord, and every man with all my heart

Pity me, shed no innocent blood — the pit

The coat, the kid of the goats, and Joseph sold
Keep the commands and show mercy to thy neighbour
Compassion toward all — not toward men only, but beasts
He shared his catch with every stranger
He that shareth with his neighbour receiveth manifold more
He clothed the naked man in winter
Have compassion, that Yahuah may have compassion on you
Joseph bore no malice — love one another
Be not divided into two heads — the two kingdoms
Led captive among the Gentiles, then He shall have mercy
Yahuah Himself, the light of righteousness, and ye shall return
Grieve not — I shall rise again in the midst of you
Truth pleases God; lying and anger teach all wickedness
The spirit of Beliar stirs up the sword against Joseph
Anger is blindness; love truth and longsuffering
Wrath joined to lying — and the Lord departs, Beliar rules

sample_cards.note: Genesis 6:4 — *There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of Elohim (God) came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.* — that the women "gave birth to giants" is the very offspring Genesis names.

Genesis 49:10 — *The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.* — that the chosen one shall "bless Yashar'el and Yahudah" and be king joins Levi's priesthood to Judah's sceptre and Shiloh.

Psalm 110:4 — *Yahuah (LORD) hath sworn, and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek).* The new priest Yahuah (the Lord) raises up, to whom all his words are revealed and who judges the earth for a multitude of days, is the priest Yahuah (the LORD) swore in after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek) — a priesthood not from Levi's line and not for a season.

sample_thread.title: The Watchers who fell through women before the flood
sample_thread.summary_md: Reuben warns against the wiles of women by recalling how the Watchers before the flood lusted after them, took the shape of men, and the women bare giants reaching even unto heaven. This is no fable of his own: it is Genesis 6 read as Enoch read it, the sons of Elohim and the daughters of men, the angels reserved in chains. It ain't new — Moses recorded it, Enoch named the Watchers, and Jude preached the same judgment.
